v.why: Adding a skip where the direct input-output path was missing restores a residual path, giving large gains (exps 22, 26, 28).
Filling an empty direct input-output edge adds both a path and capacity, giving big gains (exps 92, 98) versus replacing an existing op.
Replacing the conv on the direct path with an identity strips capacity, which is catastrophic in weak cells (exps 24, 25, 27).
Swapping a parameter-free pooling op on the final edge for a conv adds needed learnable capacity (exps 17, 18, 20).
When the parallel edge is a parameter-free skip, the cell depends more heavily on edge 0 for learned features (exps 35, 36, 40).
With edge 0 absent, edge 3 is a critical route from the input, so deleting it is far more damaging (exps 2, 10).
Without the direct input-output edge, edge 1 may be the only remaining path, so removing it severely degrades or disconnects the cell (exps 58, 60).
When edge 3 is missing, edge 5 carries most of the signal to the output, so removing it is very harmful (exps 72, 73).
If edge 1 is absent, deleting edge 0 leaves node 2 with no input and collapses the network (exp 84).
Without the direct input-output edge, the node1-to-output edge carries the main signal, so downgrading it to pooling costs more (exps 46, 47).

raw:
Each hypothesis below is a conditional (interaction) effect. The choices draw on two things: what the cell's wiring implies about paths through the network, and the 100 measured edits.

**Structural reasoning:**
- **Edge 3 is the direct input→output path.** When it is `none`, adding any working operation there restores a path that skips the whole cell. Experiments 22, 26, 28, 92 and 98 all show large gains, especially on ImageNet16-120.
- **The same edge hurts when it already holds a conv.** Replacing a `nor_conv_3x3` on edge 3 with `skip_connect` loses capacity on the main path (experiments 24, 25, 27).
- **Removing an edge is worst when it is the last path left.** If edge 3 is `none`, deleting edge 1 or edge 5 can cut node 0 off from node 3 (experiments 58, 60, 72). Likewise, if edge 1 is `none`, deleting edge 0 leaves node 2 with no input (experiment 84). Deleting edge 3 when edge 0 is `none` is similarly damaging (experiments 2, 10).
- **Adding a conv helps most in cells with no parameters.** Putting `nor_conv_3x3` on edge 5 or edge 0 gains most when the parent is made of skip and pooling operations (experiments 16–18, 20, 35, 36, 40).
- **Pooling on edge 4 hurts more when edge 3 is `none`.** In that case the edge-4 path carries much more of the signal, so pooling it costs more (experiments 46, 47).
